newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico rocked by earthquake, no damage reports.
newsitem.headline: Mexico rocked by earthquake, no damage reports.

text.p: An earthquake measuring an estimated 5.6 on the open-ended Richter scale shook southern Mexico on Tuesday, causing alarm but no immediate reports of damage, authorities said.
The Geophysics Institute of Mexico's National Autonomous University said the quake measured 5.6 and its epicentre was some 220 miles (352 km) southeast of Mexico City on the coast of Oaxaca state.
Other geologists' estimates were lower. Don Hays of the U.S. Geological Survey in Reston, Va., said the quake was 4.9 on the Richter scale.

In the state capital Oaxaca, a government spokeswoman said she did not even feel the earth movement, that begun at 3:21 p.m. (2121 GMT) and lasted almost a minute. In neighbouring Guerrero state capital Chilpancingo it was only lightly felt.
Residents living near the epicentre at Pinotepa Nacional in Oaxaca said they saw no immediate damage.
In Mexico City, the quake was felt in many parts and radio and television channels broke into normal programming to report it. Announcers said there was no visible damage in the capital.

Mexico City, in a geologically unstable area, was rocked on Jan. 11 by a powerful earthquake measuring 7.3 on the open-ended Richter scale. No damage was caused in the capital but Arteaga, a small town in the western state of Michoacan, was seriously hit.
